content.body:
The Mk IF version of the Blenheim was adapted as heavy fighter/attack aircraft from the light bomber it had started out as. A belly pack of standard fighter aircraft light machine guns (4 x .303 inch caliber) in the bomb bay cavity in addition to externally mounted 40 pound anti-personnel/light vehicle bombs was intended to equip it as an ground attack or light intruder aircraft ... as it was not a very successful level bomber.
Unfortunately, it proved to be very vulnerable against the 109s and 110s of the Luftwaffe when they finally met in combat, and was eventually withdrawn into alternative service as a night fighter where it would be unlikely to meet other fighter aircraft and perhaps fare better. Carrying their small bomb load; in addition to the machine gun package being fairly light in firepower ... Blen Mk.I's were able to play a role as light interdiction and support aircraft only during the early years of the war. They were simply not versatile enough nor did they perform well enough to excell in any combat role in general. They do make useful bomber interceptors if the bombers are unescorted and the Blenheim's have gotten to altitude early enough to make the interception, in a sense the same as the Bf110 went on to do for the Germans later in the war when Bf110's were not competitive at any other form of air combat.
Bf110's of course have a lot more firepower than Blen.I's do.
content.brief: TYPE: Heavy Fighter/Intruder-CAS WEIGHT: 5629 kg MAX SPEED: 390 km/h ARMAMENT: 6 x .303 cal. LMG 145 kg bomb load
content.title: Blenheim Mk.If Intruder
